v2.6.10 Android Automotive · MG4 Electric (SAIC)

MG4Control Advanced settings for the MG4 Electric

The community app that brings your MG4's driving, safety and comfort settings together on the head unit, with profiles, shortcuts on the car's physical buttons (steering wheel, front panel…) and automations.

Download the latest release Explore the app Installation

Explore the app

Click a feature: the mockup shows the matching screen and flashes the element in question. The mockup itself is fully clickable, and the virtual vehicle (button at the bottom right) simulates speed, temperature, Bluetooth, doors and the steering-wheel buttons.

This mockup is a simulation built for the website. The app installed in the car may look slightly different (sizes, fonts, spacing, firmware-specific details), and the values shown are examples.

Dashboard

Driving

Drive mode and regeneration, one tap away.

Drive mode

ECO, NORMAL, SPORT, SNOW or CUSTOM, with one colour per mode.

Learn more

The active mode lights up green for ECO, amber for SPORT and blue for the others. The state is re-read from the vehicle each time the screen shows. If the vehicle is not ready yet, the app retries every 3 s.

A rail tab whose page has no content on your firmware is simply hidden. Pick UNKNOWN above the mockup to watch it disappear.

Regeneration

Six levels, from Off to One Pedal, sent to the vehicle straight away.

Learn more

Off, Low, Medium, High, Adaptive and One Pedal. In SNOW, no level can be changed (not even One Pedal) and the Energy saving button is greyed out: both modes are mutually exclusive. The UI reflects these rules instead of letting you send a command the car would reject.

Energy saving

While it's on, only One Pedal remains available for regeneration.

Learn more

Toggle button under CUSTOM. Try it in the mockup: turn it on, then try changing the regeneration.

Custom mode

In CUSTOM, a card sets power, steering and pedal.

Learn more

The card appears as soon as the car is in CUSTOM, even if set from the stock screen: Power (Eco / Normal / Sport), Steering and Pedal (Comfort / Normal / Sport). A row the vehicle doesn't report disappears.

Battery heating

Smart battery heating switches on and off from the app.

Learn more

It improves fast charging but reduces range. The state is re-read from the car, including when you switch it on from the stock screen. The “Battery heating switch-off” automation turns it off after an adjustable driving time, and the action is also available as a shortcut.

Dashboard

Safety and ADAS

Driver aids, adapted to each firmware. Switch firmware above the mockup to watch the cards change.

ADAS selector

Off, manual or automatic limiter, ACC, and ICA or TJA depending on firmware.

Learn more

ICA on SWI133 and SWI132, TJA on SWI68, 69, 131 and 165. On “VSM” firmwares the limiter and ACC/TJA are two independent systems: the single selector enforces exclusivity, picking one turns the other off.

Traffic signs and sound alerts

Traffic sign recognition everywhere, plus speed alerts on SWI133 and SWI132.

Learn more

On SWI133/SWI132: overspeed alert and speed-limit change alert, greyed out and forced OFF when TSR is off, then restored when it's back on. Elsewhere: a single audible warning.

Forward collision (AEB)

On/off, alert only or with automatic braking, and sensitivity.

Learn more

Alert or Alert + auto braking mode, Low / Standard / High sensitivity. Mode buttons are greyed out while the system is off.

Lane keeping

Alert, assist or emergency keeping, with adjustable sensitivity.

Learn more

Turning the assist back on restores the last mode used. On SWI132: no emergency keeping, but two extra switches, audible warning and vibration.

ESC and drowsiness

ON / OFF buttons confirmed by re-reading the vehicle state.

Learn more

The buttons express an intent, then the app re-reads the state 700 ms later and that reading decides which one lights up. Unreadable state = no button lit, rather than a guessed state. In a profile, ESC and drowsiness are only written if that profile configures them.

Drowsiness sensitivity

Low, Standard or High, also adjustable from a physical-button shortcut.

Turning ESC off also turns the forward collision system off: the vehicle enforces it. Both return to ON at every start-up.

Dashboard

Comfort and climate

Seats, wheel and climate in one place. These settings are never blocked by the speed lock.

Heated seats and wheel

Wheel On/Off and seats on 3 levels, on equipped trims.

Learn more

The card only shows on equipped trims: SWI69 and SWI131 (Standard/SE versions) as well as SWI132 don't display it. A seat shortcut moves one step per press, in the car's own order: Off, 3, 2, 1, Off. Choosing a level on screen reaches it without running a full cycle.

Setpoint and fan

Two sliders whose bounds are read from the vehicle.

Learn more

Bounds vary between firmwares. While dragging, a single write is sent at the end, then the app re-reads the state 700 ms later. It never moves a slider under your finger.

Controls and recirculation

Power, A/C, AUTO and recirculation, kept in sync with the stock screen.

Learn more

While the screen is shown, the app follows changes made on the stock screen every 2 s. An unreadable state greys the button out rather than lying. In AUTO, the car sets the fan speed and the air direction by itself: the level shows “AUTO”, and setting the fan speed by hand leaves that mode.

Air direction

Face, feet and windshield combine, and the rear window has its own button.

Learn more

Replaces the defrost buttons. The last lit button can't be switched off: the air has to come out somewhere. Each press starts from the state read from the car.

Automatic high beam

Automatic high-beam control switches on in one tap, in the Lighting card.

Learn more

The setting is re-read from the car. It can also be part of a profile, where it only applies if you ticked it, and be driven by a shortcut on a physical button.

Climate ECO modeNew · 2.6.10

An ECO button joins A/C and AUTO: on the dashboard, in profiles and in the HVAC pop-up.

Learn more

The car's ECO mode saves climate energy. In a profile, the ECO row is On, Off or Unchanged: existing profiles leave it alone. In the HVAC pop-up, the ECO tile sits next to A/C. The state is re-read from the car.

Airflow in AUTONew · 2.6.10

In AUTO mode, pick how strong the fan runs: Low, Medium or High.

Learn more

The car's setting comes to the dashboard, to profiles, to a shortcut (“Airflow in AUTO: cycle”, floating button included) and to the HVAC pop-up. There, a tap on AUTO turns it on or off; held for 1 s, by touch or with the joystick, it steps the airflow one notch (Low → Medium → High → Low) without touching AUTO. Three notches under “AUTO” always show the airflow, even with AUTO off. If the car doesn't report this setting, a message says so.

What AUTO controlsNew · 2.6.10

Decide whether AUTO also picks the air direction and recirculation, or leaves them to you.

Learn more

In Settings › Advanced. In AUTO, the car sets the fan (always), the air direction and recirculation: untick what you want to keep, and MG4Control puts it back right after AUTO starts. And when you leave AUTO from MG4Control, the previous air direction and recirculation come back, unless you changed them in the meantime.

Top bar

Profiles

A profile applies a set of settings all at once: in one tap, from a button in the car, or automatically at start-up depending on the connected phone or the temperature.

Try:

Profile list

Up to 10 profiles (5 before 2.6.9), with a summary, a default profile and instant apply.

Learn more

Each card shows the name, a summary (mode · regeneration · ADAS) and the DEFAULT badge, with Apply now, Edit, Set default and Delete (with confirmation). The summary only lists what the profile applies: a category that is switched off is left out. Beyond five profiles, the picker scrolls its cards and the “Profile cycle” page moves to two rows.

Profile order

Long-press a profile, then drag it into place: the list order is the picker's order.

Learn more

The card lifts and follows your finger, the list scrolls by itself near its edges, and a banner shows the position it will land in; the order is saved on release. This order is the profile picker's, the “Profile cycle” page buttons' and the default cycle's (a composed cycle keeps its own). In a Bluetooth conflict it is also the priority: when the delay runs out, the first of the conflicting profiles is applied. Try it in the mockup: long-press a card in the Profiles tab.

Full-screen editor

The dashboard's three tabs, in a dedicated editor.

Learn more

The profile name and “default profile” stay visible at the top. Cancel / Save at the bottom; a name is required.

A profile never forces the unexpected: settings added over time (ESC, drowsiness, heating…) count as “not configured” in older profiles and are not written. So an old profile never disables ESC by omission.

Pick your categories

One switch per tab: switched off, the profile leaves that category alone.

Learn more

At the top of each editor tab (Driving, Safety, Comfort), an “Apply … settings” switch decides whether the profile handles it. Switched off, the tab folds away and the profile writes nothing there: the car keeps its current settings. A profile can then cover safety only, or comfort only. The tab's settings are kept and come back when you switch it on again; the rail shows “OFF” under a category that is switched off.

Existing profiles keep all three categories on, and a new profile opens with all three switched on. At least one is needed to save. Bluetooth pairing stays available even when Comfort is switched off.

Regeneration unchanged

A switch on regeneration: when off, the profile touches neither the regeneration level nor one-pedal driving.

Learn more

In the editor, Driving page. Handy for a profile that changes the drive mode, safety or comfort while keeping the regeneration chosen at the wheel. The level buttons grey out, a sentence below recalls it, and both the profile list and the picker show it (“Regen unchanged”). Existing profiles keep their regeneration.

Heating “apply” switch

Unchecked, the profile leaves the seat or wheel as it is instead of turning it off.

Learn more

Handy for a “motorway” profile that shouldn't switch off a seat already on.

Bluetooth pairing

At start-up, if the paired phone is connected, its profile applies.

Learn more

The app checks the connected phones when the infotainment starts and every time the car switches to READY. Connecting a phone mid-trip applies nothing: its profile will apply at the next switch to READY. In the virtual vehicle, connect “Pixel 8” then simulate a start-up: the “Motorway” profile gets applied.

Climate in the profile

Optional block: power, A/C, setpoint, fan, recirculation and air direction.

Learn more

In the Comfort tab, unchecked by default (older profiles leave climate alone). Setpoint from 15 to 33 °C, fan from 1 to 11, and “Unchanged” to leave a setting alone. Climate off: nothing else is written. In AUTO, the fan speed isn't applied. At start-up, if the last applied profile carries this block, its climate settings win: the temperature A/C automation doesn't apply.

Custom mode in the profile

A profile in CUSTOM also stores power, steering and pedal.

Learn more

They are only written when the profile's mode is CUSTOM. A profile saved before this feature writes nothing until it is reopened and saved.

Backup in the car

Profiles are copied to the car and can be restored after a reinstall.

Learn more

File MG4Control/mg4_profiles_backup.json in the vehicle's storage. On reinstall, if the app has no profile, a window lists the profiles found and offers to restore them.

Which profile at start-up?

When the infotainment starts and every time the car switches to READY, MG4Control picks a single profile following this precedence. Tick the situations to see which one wins.

1Recent manual choice (profile picker, app, API)
2Outside-temperature automation
3Profile tied to the connected Bluetooth device (several: restricted picker, the 1st when the delay runs out)
4Default profile

Floating window

Profile picker and brightness

Assigned to a physical button (steering wheel, front panel…), this window pops up over any app: switch profile or brightness without leaving navigation.

Brightness in one move

Night, Medium, Day and a thick slider, easy to hit while driving.

Learn more

Presets at 15%, 50% and 100%; the one matching the current brightness stays lit. 5% floor: the screen can never be switched off by mistake.

Your profiles as cards

One card per profile, with its drive mode in colour and the current profile marked “Active”: a tap applies the profile and closes the window.

Learn more

Each card shows the profile's mode (Eco, Normal, Sport, Snow, Custom) and regeneration. Up to five profiles, the cards share the width; beyond that, the row scrolls by touch or with the joystick, and the sixth card peeks over the edge to show it. The window opens on the active profile: its card is on screen and the joystick starts from it — except in a Bluetooth conflict, where it starts from the first one, the one the delay applies. That manual choice takes priority at the next ignition, unless the “Return to the default profile each time the car enters READY” option is on. The picker shows whatever the speed (it's also used for brightness); it's the write that gets filtered by the speed lock.

Auto close

The window closes by itself after an adjustable delay (10 s by default), counted down at the top right. Open MG4Control and Power the car off sit below the cards.

Bluetooth conflict

Several paired phones connected at start-up? The picker only shows their profiles.

Learn more

Without a choice before the countdown ends, the first one is applied.

Joystick navigation

The steering wheel's right joystick moves through the window, the centre confirms.

Learn more

Needs the accessibility service: a hint at the top of the window recalls the gestures, or warns that the joystick is inactive. Focus ring with no wrap-around at the edges; left/right on the slider adjust brightness in 5% steps. The joystick then changes neither volume nor track. The automation confirmation banner (NO / YES) works the same way: YES is preselected, left/right switch buttons, the centre confirms. Try it with ▲▼◀▶● in the virtual vehicle.

Close with a second press

The shortcut that opens the picker closes it again; the HVAC pop-up does the same.

Learn more

A second press on the same button closes the window just like the end of the delay: in a Bluetooth conflict, the first profile offered is applied. If that shortcut is a long press on a right-joystick key, a short press on that key still moves through the window, and a held press closes it without changing anything — on the HVAC pop-up, neither the temperature nor the fan speed moves. In the mockup, the left ★ of the virtual vehicle opens and closes the picker.

Top bar

★ button shortcuts

The steering wheel's two ★ buttons trigger the action of your choice, out of nearly fifty.

Try:

Classic ★ shortcuts

Left ★ and right ★, each with a single and a long press.

Learn more

They rely on the signal broadcast by the vehicle: if the stock launcher already uses that button, it keeps priority (e.g. 360° camera on single press). Disable the shortcut on the launcher side then.

Comfort and safety actions re-read the vehicle state on every press: an unreadable state means doing nothing, nothing is ever written blind.

Settings on demand

One Pedal, ADAS, regeneration cycle and profile cycle get their page as soon as the action is assigned.

Learn more

One Pedal fallback regen: the level restored on the second press (High by default). ADAS alternation: the two modes the button toggles between (ACC ↔ Off by default).

Regeneration cycle

Compose the order of levels a button steps through, One Pedal included.

Learn more

Tap the modes in the wanted order, tap again to remove, then Save (at least two modes). A global setting, for every button. Without it: Low → Medium → High → Adaptive, as before.

New actions

A/C, automatic high beam and battery heating join the list.

Learn more

The One Pedal, energy saving, traffic sign and sound alert toggles now start from the state read from the car: the first press after start-up always acts, even if a profile had already changed the setting.

HVAC pop-up

Climate in one move, on top of the current screen: the right joystick sets temperature and fan speed.

Learn more

A shortcut action opens the window, including when Android Auto or CarPlay fills the screen and hides the climate bar. Here the joystick moves no focus: up/down change the temperature, left/right the fan speed, the centre toggles AUTO mode (adjusting the fan speed leaves it) and, held for 1 s, steps the airflow in AUTO. At fan level 1, pressing left turns the climate off (the fan shows “OFF”); while it is off, left does nothing, and right turns it back on as it was before, at the same level or in AUTO, like changing the temperature does. The “Climate: fan +” shortcut does the same. A hint at the top of the window recalls these gestures, and a gauge shows the temperature between its two limits. A/C, recirculation and the air direction (face, feet, front and rear screen) are chosen by touch; on equipped firmwares (SWI133, SWI68, SWI165), a column adds the heated steering wheel and the seats, whose level is picked with one tap, one colour per level: green, orange, red. The window closes by itself after the set delay (10 s by default) without action, on a second press of the shortcut or with its cross. The joystick needs the accessibility service; without it, the window still works by touch. In the mockup, the right ★ of the virtual vehicle opens and closes it.

Profile cycle

One button steps through your profiles, in the order you composed.

Learn more

Tap the profiles in the wanted order, tap again to remove, then Save (at least two profiles). A global setting, for every button. Without it: every profile, in the order of their list. On each press, the shortcut targets the profile that follows the active one (the first of the cycle if the active profile is not part of it) and shows its name; it applies it one second later, then confirms it on screen. Two quick presses therefore skip a profile without applying it. A deleted profile leaves the cycle. The profiles sit in rows of five: the second row only appears from the sixth profile. If the driving safety lock refuses the write, nothing changes. In the mockup, the right ★ of the virtual vehicle steps through the profiles.

Audio source cycle

One button switches to the next audio source, in the order you composed: radio, Bluetooth, USB, online, CarPlay / Android Auto.

Learn more

In the Shortcuts tab, “Source cycle” page, tap the tiles in the wanted order (each one shows its rank), tap again to remove, then Save (at least two sources). Without it: radio then Bluetooth. On each press, “Source: …” shows and the car switches to it one second later; two quick presses therefore skip a source. There is no “change source” command: the app asks the target source to play, which brings it to the front, without pausing anything. Availability is not checked: a source with nothing to play (no USB stick, no phone) stays silent, and the next press moves on, because the cycle starts again from the last source chosen, not from the one playing. CarPlay and Android Auto go through the original receiver; if it has no phone, the app tries wireless Android Auto through DiAuto-MG4. On SWI69, SWI131 and SWI132, USB targets the port the stick is plugged into, and “Online” is not offered: that source does not exist there. In the mockup, the right ★ of the virtual vehicle steps through the sources, and the virtual vehicle shows the current source.

Android Auto / CarPlayNew · 2.6.10

One button opens Android Auto or CarPlay depending on the connected phone; a second press takes you back to the previous screen.

Learn more

MG4Control asks the car's projection service which phone is plugged in, then opens the right app. Without a phone, a message says so.

Floating buttonsNew · 2.6.10

Up to 6 bubbles on top of every app: a tap triggers the shortcut, a long press moves the bubble.

Learn more

Shortcuts tab, “Floating buttons” page. Each bubble uses one of the steering-wheel shortcut actions, with a title (the shortcut's name by default), a size, a text size and optional bold text. A toggle shows filled when it is on; a value (temperature, fan, regeneration…) shows briefly after the press, and a halo confirms the tap. A bubble can also sit in the black bar at the top of the screen. Each profile has its own bubbles, which can be copied to other profiles. They hide in reverse, in Garage mode and while Car keeper is running.

Custom shortcutsNew · 2.6.10

Create your own actions: open an app or one of its functions, send a broadcast, open a link or call a webhook.

Learn more

Shortcuts tab, “Custom shortcuts” page (20 at most), with a Test button. They can then be assigned to the steering-wheel buttons, advanced shortcuts and floating buttons. The functions offered are the Android shortcuts of installed apps and the ones their developers expose to MG4Control (action com.mg4.control.action.SHORTCUT). Webhooks over HTTPS only; system targets are refused.

Shortcuts

Advanced shortcuts: any key

Almost every physical button in the car, not just the steering wheel: steering-wheel keys, front-panel keys below the screen… as a short, long or double press. Created in three steps: key, press type, action.

Path:

Accessibility service

Enabled once in Android. At rest, it consumes no key.

Learn more

Through it, MG4Control sees the key before the launcher and can consume it. The “Enable accessibility” button opens Android's service list and disappears once access is granted.

Record a key

Tap “Record a key” then the wanted button.

Learn more

Any button whose press reaches the screen can be used. Its name and code show up (left ★ 17, right ★ 286, joystick 297 to 301…); a button with no known name shows its code (“Key 123”) and still works. Tapping the record button again cancels; the wait also times out on its own.

Shortcut list

Grouped by button and press type, with a confirmation before replacing an action.

Learn more

“All profiles” first in each group (display order is resolution order). Edit changes the action and the profile. The confirmation names the action about to be replaced.

Profile-scoped shortcuts

One button does a different thing depending on the current profile.

Learn more

Example: under Motorway, right ★ toggles One Pedal; under Winter, it sets the heated seat. Each shortcut carries a profile (“All profiles” by default).

The profile that counts is the last applied profile, however it was applied: at start-up, over Bluetooth, by the temperature automation or by hand. MG4Control remembers it even after a restart. Changing a setting by hand on the dashboard, however, doesn't change that profile. The virtual vehicle shows the current profile.

On press, that profile's shortcut comes first, otherwise the “All profiles” one. A key is only intercepted if it carries an action for that profile.

Presses without a shortcut kept

A press without a shortcut keeps the button's original function.

Learn more

The press is returned to the system. Assigning the Home button's double press therefore leaves its single press returning to the launcher. The only cost: a 0.3 s delay on a key carrying a double press. In Garage mode, every key is released.

Press lab: short, long or double?

Hold a button: the long press fires at 500 ms, key still held. On a key that also carries a double press, the short press waits another 300 ms. Create an advanced shortcut first to see the difference.

Steering-wheel shortcut

Car keeper

The car stays on and locked while you're away: to cool it down or warm it up before you return, for a pet left on board, or to watch over it with a 360° camera.

Pre-conditioningNew · 2.6.10

Climate right away or at a set time, in cycles, with the temperature and fan level of your choice.

Learn more

The “Car keeper” shortcut opens a window that always starts on “Now”: the climate runs for at most 15 min, 30 min, 1 h or 2 h. “At a time” schedules the first cycle, its length, the number of cycles and the pause between them; the climate stays off while waiting. The car must be in P. Get out with the key: after an adjustable countdown, MG4Control locks the doors itself (locking with the key would switch the car off); before getting out, switch the lights and wipers to OFF yourself: the app doesn't do it. The floating buttons disappear from the countdown until the end. At the end, the climate goes back to its previous settings and the car switches off. Unlocking stops everything and leaves the car on; it also stops by itself below an adjustable battery level or if the car moves.

Dog modeNew · 2.6.10

For a pet left on board: climate for 2 h, and a reassuring message for passers-by.

Learn more

Dog mode is picked under “Now”. The screen stays on and shows, in large type, a message that all is well, the set temperature, the outside one, how long the climate has been running and the battery level. A warning reminds you to check regularly that the mode is still active: a battery that is too low, locking with the key or a fault would stop the climate.

Surveillance modeNew · 2.6.10

With a 360° camera app, the car stays awake and locked to record, with the climate off.

Learn more

Only offered if the camera app (MG4-360-Camera-App or its MG4_Dashcam version) is installed. Duration up to 2 h; only the screen and the cameras draw power, about 0.2 kW. The screen shows, in a fixed red frame, “CAMERA SURVEILLANCE” and a notice that the vehicle is being filmed all around. Same stops as pre-conditioning: low battery, unlocking or the car moving. Your climate settings are restored at the end.

Follow-up screenNew · 2.6.10

Full screen: time left, current cycle and lock state, with blue or orange particles depending on whether the climate cools or heats.

Learn more

While waiting, the screen stays normal, dims (the default) or turns off; a touch lights it for 10 s, and Hide / Stop stay within reach. On SWI133, SWI68 and SWI165, a card on the driver display also shows the countdown, the time left and the setpoint, or the surveillance in progress (switch on the Car keeper page of the Shortcuts tab).

Top bar

Automations

One tab, eight automations. Each has its own switch, and its card unfolds when you turn it on.

Try:

Profile by temperature

Above or below a threshold, a profile applies, directly or after confirmation.

Learn more

Threshold from 0 to 60 °C, inclusive. A banner at the bottom of the screen asks the question for the set delay (10 s by default), without hiding navigation: it shows the reading, the threshold and the profile, and is answered by touch or with the steering wheel's right joystick. NO or timeout falls back to the Bluetooth or default profile. Unreadable temperature or deleted profile: the automation is skipped.

Climate by temperature

Two rules side by side, hot and cold, are set with sliders and switch the climate on with your settings.

Learn more

By default: from 28 °C outside → 20 °C, up to 5 °C outside → 24 °C. Each rule has its own switch and sliders: outside threshold (−20 to 60 °C), setpoint and fan level within the car's own limits. The fan is automatic or manual; front and rear defrost and recirculation (unchanged, inner, outside or auto) are picked with buttons. The cold threshold always stays below the hot one. If the last applied profile carries its own climate settings, those win.

A/C: when to trigger

Three modes: at start-up only, once per start, or each time the car enters READY.

Learn more

By default, a single check is made when the car starts (READY): if the threshold is not met at that moment, nothing triggers until the next full start of the car. With “Once per start”, the check is repeated each time the car enters READY again; as soon as the threshold is met, the settings are applied once, then nothing more until the next full start of the car. “Each time the car enters READY” sends the settings every time, including after a short stop. In the mockup, “Leave the car” then “Back to READY” replay a stop during a trip.

Profile by battery level

When the battery drops below a threshold, a profile applies, directly or after confirmation.

Learn more

Threshold from 5 to 60%. It triggers once, at start-up or while driving, then re-arms at the next start-up or after charging above the threshold. Try it with the Battery slider of the virtual vehicle.

Automatic brightness

The screen brightens by day and dims at night, in a garage or in a tunnel.

Learn more

Two sources to choose from: the headlights coming on, with no mobile data at all, and the Open-Meteo forecast, which estimates outside light for about 10 KB per download. The adjustment happens when entering READY, and optionally while driving. A manual adjustment pauses the automation until the next start-up. The mockup shows the “lights only” version.

Battery heating switch-off

Battery heating turns itself off after an adjustable driving time.

Learn more

From 5 to 120 minutes, 30 by default. The countdown starts when heating is switched on, wherever from, or at start-up if it already was.

SoundsNew · 2.6.10

Your own sounds, imported from a USB stick, played at chosen moments and at the volume you want.

Learn more

Moments: MG4Control start-up, entering or leaving READY, shifting to P or D, front door opened (SWI133 and SWI132) and profile applied. As many sounds as moments, each moment belonging to one sound only. The file (MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, WAV or FLAC, 30 s at most) is copied into the app, so the stick can be removed afterwards. The car's media volume is set for the length of the sound, then given back. A trigger during playback is ignored, and sounds can be kept to some profiles.

Climate: air directionNew · 2.6.10

The climate-by-temperature rules also pick the air direction.

Learn more

An Air row joins each rule: an air direction, or Unchanged. It is applied last, after the fan; with the automatic fan, the chosen air direction and recirculation are set again right after AUTO starts, then checked.

Automation

Power windows

Every window closes automatically when you leave the car, and opens or closes at the press of a physical button. On all six firmwares.

Try:

Close all, open all

Every window in one press, from a physical button or the external API.

Learn more

The driver's window runs its native automatic travel. The other three, which have no sensor, get the command for the travel time. Close all and Open all are physical-button shortcuts and external API commands; the on-screen buttons have been removed.

Travel time

Windows without a sensor move for an adjustable time: 5 s by default, from 2 to 10 s.

Learn more

Only the driver's window reports its position. For the other three, the app can't tell when the window reaches its end stop: it sends the command for this long. Too short and the window stays ajar, and a tired rear window may need a little more. Five seconds is the value winclose uses on the MG4.

Close when leaving the car

Every window closes when you get out, after an adjustable delay.

Learn more

Car in P and closing armed (speed reached, 20 km/h by default, and/or car on for 5 min). When leaving READY (seat belt unfastened and driver door opened, or car switched off), closing after 0 to 30 s (5 s by default), with an optional beep. Going back to READY cancels. Windows without a sensor close for the travel time.

Per-window calibration (advanced)

Optionally, a wizard times each window for a more accurate travel time than the general one.

Learn more

The 4-step wizard times a full descent and ascent (between 0.8 and 15 s), then that window uses its own times. Turning the option off goes back to the general travel time without erasing the measurements. The app can't see the door switches: a travel always lasts the measured time, whatever the window's starting position.

Travels commanded by the app have no anti-pinch protection, except on the driver's window. Keep everyone clear of the windows during a closing, especially an automatic one. Window control builds on winclose (Skittle6938).

Automation

Volume when leaving the car

No more blasting music as you step out of the car.

Try:

Volume drop

Media volume drops to the chosen level when you get out. The card has moved to the Automation tab.

Learn more

On SWI133 and SWI132, which report their doors, the trigger stays a front door opening. Elsewhere it's leaving READY in P (seat belt unfastened and driver door opened, or car switched off). The slider is capped to the real maximum volume read from the car. Selected firmware: .

Doors and restore

Pick the trigger doors, and get the previous volume back when closing.

Learn more

Left, right or both, handy to react to the driver's door only. Without readable doors (other than SWI133/132), this choice disappears and the restore happens when going back to READY.

Or pauseNew · 2.6.10

Instead of lowering the volume, the card can pause the media, then resume playback.

Learn more

The card is now called “Media when leaving the car”. In pause mode, the media is only stopped if it was playing, and playback only resumes (when the door closes, or back in READY without readable doors) if MG4Control was the one that paused it.

Top bar

Statistics

Trips, charging and cost. Off by default; everything stays in the car, nothing is sent anywhere.

Try:

General

Summary over 30 days or all history: distance, consumption, energy and cost.

Learn more

kWh price for slow and fast charging (up to 100,000, for every currency), currency, retention (30 days to 1 year) and “Delete all”. A period's consumption is computed on totals, and a trip's cost follows the average price of energy actually charged. The mockup's data are examples.

Battery and state of health

Pick your battery among the MG4's three, enter its state of health (SOH), and skip trips that are too short.

Learn more

51, 64 or 77 kWh, then the state of health, from 50 to 100% in 0.5% steps, with the − and + buttons (hold them to scroll). The capacity used, usable capacity × state of health, shows below: it converts a charge into kWh, and changing either recalculates the charges already recorded. Leave 100% if you don't know the state of health: a dealer or an OBD app can measure it. Until the battery is confirmed, the Charging tab reminds you. The short-trip filter is off by default; when on, a trip shorter than the chosen distance (1 km by default) is no longer recorded.

Trips

Each trip with its duration, distance, consumption and energy breakdown.

Learn more

A trip runs from one ignition to the next. On SWI133 and SWI132, the breakdown comes from the car's counters: motor, climate, accessories and regeneration. Other firmwares have no such counters: energy is computed from the battery voltage and current, and the breakdown is limited to “Motor” and “Climate control and others”, in whole kWh. Switch firmware above the mockup to compare. Selected firmware: .

Charging

Energy charged, cost and AC / DC sessions, even while the head unit was off.

Learn more

An overnight charge is reconstructed on wake-up; you can complete it (plug type, times) to get the average power, and fix the tariff of a session. Both are entered without a keyboard, with − and + buttons: hours and minutes (in steps of five) for the times, a step of your choice for the tariff.

Fast-charge energy

On a fast charge, energy is measured during the charge instead of being worked out from the percentage, and each charge's details say where its energy figure comes from.

Learn more

On a fast charge, the displayed percentage doesn't track the energy going in: on a charge from 62.8 to 70.1%, 5.0 kWh were measured at the battery, while the percentage difference only accounted for 4.2. So the app measures the energy during the charge, even with the charging pop-up turned off. The head unit turns off when the car is locked: a charge seen in part is measured over what was seen and estimated for the rest, a charge never seen is estimated, both from a table learnt 1% band by 1% band over the fast charges it follows (a band is used from two measurements, recent ones weigh more). The details say so: “measured during the charge”, “partly measured”, “estimated from previous charges” or “estimated from the battery level”. AC charges are still computed from the percentage, and a measured energy no longer changes when you change the battery or the state of health.

Pop-up · Settings · Interface

Charging

As soon as a charge starts, a pop-up opens on the head unit: the curve since the start of the charge, the end time, the charge limit to set by touch, and the cost. On every firmware, off by default.

Try:

Charging pop-up

The battery to a tenth, the power and level curve, then power, energy added, range gained, cost and duration.

Learn more

It opens at the start of every charge, AC or fast, even when the app starts in the middle of a charge, and closes on demand or when the car goes to READY: no countdown. The curve starts at the beginning of the charge, not when the pop-up opens: the app logs the charge in the background (a gap if the screen turns off), the kW axis goes up to the highest power reached, and a dotted line joins the current level to the limit at the estimated end time. Range gained is the change in the car's estimated range since the start. The “Charging pop-up” shortcut reopens or closes it; the option is turned on in Settings › Interface. In the mockup, plug in a charger from the virtual vehicle: the charge runs fast-forward, and goes into Statistics when unplugged.

Charge limit by touch

The battery bar becomes a slider: from 40 to 100% in steps of 10, the limit goes to the car on release, and the end time follows.

Learn more

Below the current level, the pop-up warns that the charge will stop; if the car doesn't take the new limit, it says so. On the A9 firmwares (SWI69, SWI131, SWI132), the limit can only be set when the car allows it, as in its own charging app: not with an LFP battery (MG4 Standard), which charges to 100%. The bar then shows the level only, a padlock explains why, and the end time aims for full. In the mockup, an A9 with the 51 kWh battery (Statistics tab) stands for the LFP battery. Selected firmware: .

Price of this charge

The cost follows the AC or DC tariff from the Statistics tab; the pencil corrects it for this charge only, without a keyboard.

Learn more

− and + buttons with a step of your choice (hold them to scroll), cost recalculated live, the old one struck through beside it. “Default tariff” goes back to the Statistics tariff. The corrected price follows the charge into the Statistics tab, like “Fix the tariff”.

Settings · Interface

Driver display

An MG4Control module in the centre of the instrument cluster, behind the wheel: live consumption or power, in a dynamic or discreet style, and the charge in progress. On SWI133, SWI68 and SWI165, off by default.

Try:

A module on the cluster

The cluster's central square, the one used by navigation and music, shows an MG4Control module instead of its original page.

Learn more

Turn on “Module on the instrument cluster” in Settings, Interface tab. The module shows as soon as the app starts, without waiting for READY, and takes the cluster's background to blend in. The cluster is a separate computer: only this 260 × 260 px square comes from the head unit, where a SAIC app draws it, and that app only exists on SWI133, SWI68 and SWI165. On the A9 firmwares (SWI69, SWI131, SWI132), the cluster draws everything itself: nothing can show there, and the card does not appear in the settings. Try the preview below the cards.

Consumption or power

Two graduated modules: the ring of live consumption, or the power arc, regeneration on the left, power on the right and instant consumption below.

Learn more

Consumption: in Wh/km or kWh/100 km, while driving, on a logarithmic scale up to 3,000 Wh/km (300 kWh/100 km) so acceleration peaks stay readable; the graduations follow the unit; when stationary, the kW drawn (climate, accessories); when regenerating, from 5 km/h, a negative consumption, in blue (25 kW recovered at 60 km/h: −41.7 kWh/100 km), the ring showing the kW recovered. Power: from 60 kW recovered to 320 kW (the XPower), on a tightened scale that makes the arc move while driving — 20 kW already fill a quarter of it —, orange while the battery drains, blue while it recharges; the fill stops cleanly at zero; whole kW while driving, and below, in large type, the instant consumption, negative and blue when regenerating. At the bottom, the trip average since READY (regeneration deducted), plus the energy recovered on the Consumption module; the battery, already on the cluster, is no longer there. At the top, a badge: the applied profile in the colour of its drive mode, or the drive mode. The figure doesn't jump from one value to the next: it counts (100, 101… 300), and the gauge glides along.

One module per tab, and a preview

One module for the Navigation tab, another (or none) for the Music tab; next to the settings, a preview on a simulated trip follows every change.

Learn more

The cluster's tabs are picked from the steering wheel, and the module follows the tab shown. Trip computer, tyre pressure and settings are drawn by the cluster itself: no module can show there. The settings come in three groups: Modules; Appearance, with the style (dynamic or discreet) and the badge (profile, drive mode or none); Units, with the gauge unit (Wh/km or kWh/100 km) and, separately, the trip-average unit, which can also be km/kWh. “Advanced” unfolds the refresh rate, from 0.1 to 1 s (1 s by default: shorter is more responsive, but the figure moves more), and the animation length, from 0.2 to 2 s (0.8 s by default), the time the gauge takes to glide from one value to the next. The drive mode and the profile are read every 10 seconds.

Discreet style

For those who find scrolling figures distracting: a thin graduated bar, fixed figures under the ticks, and the trip average at the bottom.

Learn more

Power: zero marked, regeneration on the left in blue, power on the right in light grey. Consumption: a short regeneration zone on the left, then the scale; an “avg” triangle marks the trip average, and the bar is green below it, orange above. Same scales as the dynamic style (60 kW of regeneration, 320 kW, 3,000 Wh/km), same badge, same average at the bottom. The bar follows over two seconds, without jitter, whatever the refresh rate. Settings › Interface › Appearance › Style.

While charging

The charge module replaces the gauge: in large type the time left to the limit, the level to a tenth and the end time, then power, energy and duration.

Learn more

It takes the gauge's place on the tabs that have a module, as soon as a charge is detected, AC or fast. The badge's lightning bolt pulses and a highlight runs along the bar up to the limit; when done, everything freezes and turns green: “Charge complete”. When unplugged, the gauge comes back. Try the preview below the cards: “⚡ DC charge” plugs in a fast charger.

Settings per profileNew · 2.6.10

Each driver gets their own driver display: pick the profiles to set, and each change applies to all the selected ones.

Learn more

At the top of the card, “Settings for:” shows every profile as chips, with multiple selection. The whole card follows the active profile, and a new profile starts with the module off.

Kilometres or milesNew · 2.6.10

A Distance row: Auto, km or miles. Auto follows the unit set in the car.

Learn more

In miles, the whole module switches: gauge in Wh/mi or kWh/100 mi, average in Wh/mi, kWh/100 mi or mi/kWh, never mixing units. Auto is the default; a choice already made is kept.

Power scale that fitsNew · 2.6.10

The power gauge fits your MG4 instead of always going up to 320 kW.

Learn more

Max power: Auto (the default), 125, 150, 180 or 320 kW, per profile. Auto learns from the peaks actually reached: the scale goes up as soon as it is exceeded, and comes down one step after five trips that stayed well below. The ticks stay whole numbers, in both the dynamic and the discreet style.

Module preview

The module as it shows in the cluster's central square, with the style, units, badge and animation set in the mockup. Driving is simulated: pick the module and the style, accelerate, brake, or plug in a charger.

Top bar

App settings

Four tabs, everything applies on tap. Change the app language in the mockup: labels come from the real translations.

Try:

Languages

Seven languages, asked on the very first launch and changeable later.

Learn more

Français, English, Deutsch, Español, Português, Italiano and Türkçe. On first launch, seven large tiles: each language is written in its own language.

Interface and text size

Start screen, Auto / Dark / Light theme and Standard, Large or Extra-large text.

Learn more

In Auto, the app follows the MG launcher's day/night mode. Pop-ups and banners (profile picker, HVAC pop-up, confirmation, update alert, power-off) take the app's theme. Text size (+12.5% or +25%) applies to the whole app, popups included, and Turkish joins the languages. Try it in the mockup.

Pop-up delay

A slider sets how long pop-ups stay open before closing by themselves, from 1 to 60 seconds.

Learn more

In Settings, Interface tab. The delay, 10 seconds by default, applies to everything that closes by itself: the profile picker, the HVAC pop-up and the three banners (YES / NO question of the automations, update alert, vehicle power-off). Each action in a pop-up restarts the delay, and the next one opened uses the new value. With no answer when the delay runs out, the question counts as NO, the update alert as “later”, and the power-off is cancelled.

Redesigned pop-ups and windows

The same look everywhere: rounded cards, large buttons, and no more keyboard input.

Learn more

On top of the car's screen, the profile picker and the HVAC pop-up are shown full frame, and three banners at the bottom of the screen — automation confirmation, update available, vehicle power-off — leave the rest usable. Inside the app, confirmations all look alike: blue for an ordinary action, orange for a warning, red for whatever deletes or powers off. An app or a profile is picked from a grid of tiles, a shortcut is edited in two side-by-side lists, and the times or tariff of a charge are set with − and + buttons.

Larger tabs

The five top-bar tabs span the full width, with text the size of the rest of the app.

Learn more

New order: Profiles, Automation, Shortcuts, Statistics, Settings. The Audio tab is gone: its card lives in Automation. In the light theme, the logo sits on a dark plate.

Advanced settings

Garage mode, back to the default profile, external API, beta channel, vehicle power-off and speed lock.

Learn more
  • Garage mode, replacing the old automatic-application switch.
  • Return to the default profile each time the car enters READY, to forget a hand-picked profile.
  • External API, with explicit confirmation when enabling.
  • Update check at launch, alert on the vehicle screen and beta channel.
  • Power the vehicle off while keeping the screen on, and speed lock (0 to 250 km/h).

Back to the default profile

An option makes the app forget a hand-picked profile each time the car enters READY.

Learn more

By default, a hand-picked profile (picker, app, shortcut) stays in place until the car is switched off: it is re-applied each time the car enters READY. With the “Return to the default profile each time the car enters READY” option in Advanced settings, it is forgotten each time the car enters READY, including after a short stop, and the default profile is applied again. A profile tied to the outside temperature or to a Bluetooth phone keeps priority, as at start-up. In the mockup: apply a profile by hand, then “Leave the car” and “Back to READY”.

Info

Updates, About, detected firmware, data usage and diagnostics.

Learn more
  • Check for updates, Clean APK (old downloaded files). Release notes show in the app's language when the release translates them, otherwise in English.
  • About: version, exact firmware, GitHub / GitLab QR codes, thanks.
  • Data usage: today, this week, this month, last 30 days.
  • Diagnostic, revealed by tapping the logo 5 times: a report to copy or download for bug reports.

Android settingsNew · 2.6.10

A button opens the Android settings screen, which the car's launcher does not offer.

Learn more

In Settings › Info, under the Info button, and as an “Android settings” shortcut action (steering wheel, advanced shortcuts, floating buttons). Depending on the firmware, it is the Android or the Android Automotive screen; if neither opens, a message says so. Thanks to @sensoyg, whose fork brought the idea.

Unrecognised firmware

A warning shows, then you can force a compatibility mode.

Learn more

The warning shows the raw detected version and offers Close the app or Continue, which opens Settings → Info directly: tap the chip of the firmware closest to yours. The choice is saved, survives restarts and applies from the app's start-up. Distributor firmwares, such as the Turkish DBI68, are recognised on their own: DBI68 counts as SWI68, DBI133 as SWI133.

Full screenNew · 2.6.10

An option hides the status bar and the navigation bar to give MG4Control the full screen height.

Learn more

In Settings › Interface, off by default. Swipe from the edge to bring the bars back for a moment.

Climate during Android Auto / CarPlayNew · 2.6.10

During projection, tapping the climate area of the top bar opens MG4Control's HVAC pop-up.

Learn more

Android Auto and CarPlay fill the screen: the climate area at the top then opens the HVAC pop-up instead of the stock panel. Switch in Settings › Interface, off by default, suspended in Garage mode.

Car languageNew · 2.6.10

On first launch, MG4Control takes the car's language if it is translated; otherwise it asks you.

Learn more

Seven languages: French, English, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Turkish. Pop-ups shown before the app is first opened follow that language too. A choice already made is left unchanged.

Advanced settings

Garage mode

One switch puts MG4Control fully to sleep, without erasing anything. Designed for leaving the car at a workshop.

Try:

What's suspended

Shortcuts, floating buttons, start-up profile, automations, external API and update alerts.

Learn more
  • Physical buttons get their original function back (classic and advanced shortcuts).
  • Floating buttons leave the screen at once.
  • No profile at start-up (Bluetooth included), no temperature automation.
  • Nothing triggers when leaving: no volume drop, no window closing.
  • Third-party commands refused, no update alert on screen.

What still works

Opening the app and applying a profile by hand. Switching back off restores everything as it was.

Learn more

While it's on, the persistent notification says MG4Control is asleep, so a forgotten mode doesn't look like a failure. Anyone who had unchecked the old “automatic application” switch is carried over with Garage mode on.

Emergency shortcutNew · 2.6.10

Hold the right joystick's centre click for 5 s: MG4Control opens, even in Garage mode.

Learn more

Handy when no icon is within reach. On by default, in Settings › Advanced; it relies on the accessibility service (advanced shortcuts). The button keeps its usual function.

Safeguards

Speed lock and power-off

The lock applies to everything that writes to the vehicle: the app, profiles, shortcuts and the external API.

Try:

Speed lock

Above the chosen speed, driving settings are refused with a message.

Learn more
  • Off by default: no limit applies until it's enabled.
  • Allowed up to the chosen speed, inclusive.
  • Unreadable speed = refusal (fail closed).
  • Comfort (seats, wheel, climate) is never affected.

Power the car off, screen on

Powers the vehicle down while keeping music and navigation, lever in P only.

Learn more

Mirrors the MG launcher's “Vehicle Power → Off”. Available in Settings, the profile picker and shortcuts. The app checks the lever before the confirmation, then again when sending. From a shortcut or the profile picker, the confirmation is a banner at the bottom of the screen: it closes by itself after the pop-up delay, and says “Cannot power off” if the car isn't in P. Deliberately left out of the external API.

Decision simulator

Replica of VehicleWriteGate.decide() for a driving setting.

Settings · Info

Built-in updates

The app checks GitHub for new releases (GitLab as fallback) and installs the APK after checking it.

Try:

Alert on the vehicle screen

A banner at the bottom of the screen announces the new release without opening the app, never while driving.

Learn more

Install update opens the usual dialog, Skip this version stops offering it, Stop telling me turns the alert off, Later closes the banner, as does no answer when the pop-up delay runs out. The rest of the screen stays usable. Check 20 s after ignition, 6 h minimum between requests, only once per session.

Stable or beta

Stable channel by default, beta channel for pre-releases.

Learn more

The stable release then replaces the latest beta of the same number, never the other way round. “Don't remind me” skips a given version.

Safe download

The APK must come from GitHub or GitLab and carry the same signature, otherwise it's deleted.

Learn more

The update window shows the release notes on the left and the actions on the right. Without Wi-Fi, a warning reminds you about 10 MB will go through the car's mobile data. Manual install is possible: QR code to the releases, a FAT32 USB stick and the file manager. The offline variant has neither network nor automatic updates.

For power users

External API: KeyMapper, Tasker, adb

A third-party app can trigger MG4Control features and read the vehicle state. Disabled by default: while it is, every command is refused and logged.

Test console

Build a command, copy it for your car, or send it to the virtual vehicle to see how the app answers. Enable the API in the mockup's Settings first.

API reference

Direct actions (KeyMapper)

No extra needed. In KeyMapper (2.3.0+): Intent action → Broadcast receiver type → paste the string. Each send flips the state.

  • com.mg4.control.action.ONE_PEDAL
  • com.mg4.control.action.ENERGY_SAVING_TOGGLE
  • com.mg4.control.action.PROFILE_PICKER
  • com.mg4.control.action.OPEN_APP

EXECUTE (every shortcut action)

Text extra action = name of a shortcut action (REGEN_CYCLE, SEAT_HEAT_LEFT_CYCLE, WINDOWS_CLOSE_ALL…). APPLY_PROFILE needs a profile extra.

Deliberately outside the API: VEHICLE_POWER_OFF, ADAS_CYCLE, AEB_CYCLE, TSR_TOGGLE, OVERSPEED_ALARM, SPEED_LIMIT_TONE, SOUND_WARNING.

SET · keyvalueNotes
drive_modeECO NORMAL SPORT SNOW CUSTOMNot cyclable.
regenOFF LOW MEDIUM HIGH ADAPTIVE ONE_PEDAL
seat_heat_left · seat_heat_right0, 1, 2, 3Cyclable (NEXT / PREV / TOGGLE).
steering_heat0/1, false/true
profileprofile nameNot cyclable.
hvac_power · ac · hvac_auto0/1Cyclable. Setpoint and fan clamped to bounds read from the vehicle.
hvac_temp · hvac_fan°C · level
hvac_recircINNER OUTSIDE AUTO
defrost_front · defrost_rear0/1

Reading the state

content://com.mg4.control.state/state (com.mg4.control.offline.state for the offline variant) returns one row with mode, regeneration, heating, speed, outside temperature, firmware and profiles. An unreadable value is null, never 0.

Security and diagnostics

Once enabled, any installed app can send these intents. Every read is logged and the external_api_allowlist preference filters packages. The speed lock applies to the API.

adb logcat -s MG4_API

Installation

Every release ships two variants: Online (standard use, automatic updates) and Offline 🔒 (no network access). Install just one.

  1. Download the APK from the GitHub releases. Already installed? Update from the app (Settings → Info).
  2. Copy it to a FAT32-formatted USB stick.
  3. Plug the stick into the MG4 and open the file manager (access to the AAOS settings).
  4. Install the APK, open MG4Control and pick your language.

Build it yourself

Android Studio Hedgehog (2023.1)+, JDK 17+, SDK API 34.

./gradlew assembleOnlineDebug
# app/build/outputs/apk/online/debug/

The app runs with the system identity (android.uid.system): it must be signed with the ROM key.
